Subject: Three things to do on trail this autumn
CTA: Share these tips with your hiking group -> https://example.com/trail-care-autumn
Body: Autumn shifts fast on trail. Leaves come down, water moves differently, and the ground softens in ways that matter.

Here are three trail-care habits worth carrying into the season:

**1. Clear water bars before the rains arrive.**
A blocked water bar can redirect enough runoff to cut a new erosion channel in a single storm. Walk your regular stretch and clear debris by hand before the heavy rain hits — not after. A folding saw or a stout stick works fine. The goal is an unobstructed outlet so water exits the trail, not travels down it.

**2. Step on the mud, not around it.**
It sounds backwards, but walking around a muddy section widens the trail. If the surface is soft, walk straight through the center. If that's genuinely not possible, wait for it to freeze or dry. Two passes around a puddle can turn a 24-inch tread into a 6-foot scar over a single season.

**3. Report blowdowns the same day you find them.**
A fresh blowdown is a 30-minute job with a crosscut saw. Leave it two weeks and roots lift, bark rots, and the work triples. Most land managers have a reporting line or app — use it the day you hit the obstacle. Include the trailhead name, distance from the trailhead, and which direction the log fell.

That's it. Nothing complicated. Just three things that keep trail open for the people coming behind you.
